supported: The CPR bars sharing Subscriber Information with uninvolved third parties unless prior consent is obtained (24.6). It strictly prohibits one use: interconnection data for other purposes, including marketing (24.7). The law punishes disclosing communication content without the right to do so (Article (72)).
unsupported: A prohibition on a Licensee using its own subscribers’ information for marketing or model training. None was found in the ingested text.

supported: The CPR says a Licensee must obtain prior consent before sharing Subscriber Information with third parties not directly involved in the ordered service (24.6). Its footnote allows contractual consent with a way to withdraw. The 2009 policy requires consent before a Licensee’s own marketing messages (5.5).
unsupported: A consent rule specific to ML training. Any inconsistency with the Data Protection Law is decided by that law (24.1), which is not in this KB.

supported: Third parties directly involved in supply are required to use the information only as required for providing the service (24.9). Interconnection data is limited to interconnection (24.7).
unsupported: A general purpose-limitation duty on a Licensee’s own use. The phrase does not occur in the ingested telecom text.

template_outcome: Refers the case to an oversight body
supported: The law names the Authority the competent body to oversee Licensees (Article (12)). A consumer can take a complaint to the TDRA as a Consumer Dispute (2.1.8, 26.16). The TDRA may request Subscriber Information in writing (24.11).
unsupported: A duty on a Licensee to refer or report a privacy breach to any body. None was found in the ingested text. The Data Protection Law and the Data Office decree returned HTTP 403 and were not read.
